messages:
mia: Kickoff: Accentor customer's LoRA merge is staged. I've pushed a quick-eval pack to s3 and added a smoke runner. Need sanity checks: int8/int4 quant, tokenizer alignment, and behavioral diffs on 5 prompts. s3://redwood-evals/accentor/pack_v1

sam: On it. Which baseline + quant profile are we comparing against?

mia: Baseline is rwd-13b-v1 FP16. Compare merged LoRA vs FP16. Targets: int8 and int4 quant configs. Quick run command: `scripts/eval_quick.sh --model merged --quant int4 --prompts 5`

jordan: Ran smoke with `--quant int8` on gpu-dedicated-02 — latency & quality look OK. Quick stats: exact_match=0.86, answer_overlap=0.91. Logs: ```./logs/accentor_int8.out
avg_latency=210ms p95=420ms
```

anita: Int4 produced a tokenizer hiccup for customer token `<ACCT_ID>` — responses truncate after that token for prompt id 3. Repro steps: open prompt 3 in pack and run `--quant int4`. Diff: ```- ...<ACCT_ID>12345
+ ...< ACCT_ID> 12345```

sam: Could be tokenizer vocab merge after the LoRA stitch. Did the merge script apply any tokenizer remap?

mia: We used default stitch flow, no explicit remap applied. I'll re-run with tokenizer aliasing enabled.

jordan: CI run for int4 failed for that prompt — short CI log: https://ci.redwood/12345 (artifacts linked)

ci-bot: Build 4821: eval-int4 FAILED; errors=1; artifacts: https://ci.redwood/4821/artifacts

anita: Quick test: adding a token alias map `{"<ACCT_ID>":"<ACCT_ID>"}` in the loader avoids the split in local repro. Will push patch to feature/alias-fix and re-run.

sam: If alias fixes it, re-run full 20-prompt pack and collect BLEU / PPL / per-token prob for the truncated token. Also capture latency with `--batch 1` and `--batch 4`.

mia: Plan: 1) apply alias remap + rerun int4; 2) run int8 and fp16 baseline full 20 prompts; 3) generate one-page quick-report for CS with metrics + recommended serving config. ETA EOD.

jordan: :thumbsup: Will queue jobs on gpu-dedicated-03 and monitor.

sam: :eyes: note: for int4 prefer `--batch 1` in smoke to avoid token-merging artifacts introduced by some batch packing kernels.

anita: If alias doesn't fix it, fallback plan is to serve Accentor on int8 until we can retrain / update tokenizer.

mia: @leo fyi — tagging CS lead for awareness.

leo: Thanks — pls ping when the one-pager is ready, CS wants to know if int4 is safe or we should lock to int8.

mia: Will do. I'll post the report + CI links here once runs finish.
